questions.q: What does password-file authentication (via orapwd) make possible that local OS authentication cannot?
options: Remote SYSDBA/SYSOPER connections, even before the database is mounted
Encrypting all network traffic to the database
Creating users without any privileges at all
Replacing the need for a data dictionary
questions.explain: OS authentication only works for local connections; the password file lets SYSDBA/SYSOPER connect remotely, which matters because that can happen before the database is even mounted.

questions.q: A user is created with IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY. What does this mean?
options: The account has no database password and relies on the operating system having already authenticated the connecting user
The account can only be accessed from a different database instance
The account's password is stored in an external file on the client machine
The account is automatically granted DBA privileges
questions.explain: IDENTIFIED EXTERNALLY accounts trust OS-level authentication instead of storing a database password.

questions.q: What is the key difference between SYS and SYSTEM in Oracle?
options: SYS owns the data dictionary and should only connect AS SYSDBA; SYSTEM is a default DBA-role account but not the dictionary owner
SYS and SYSTEM are simply two names for the same account
SYSTEM owns the data dictionary; SYS is only for read-only reporting
SYS is used only in test environments, SYSTEM only in production
questions.explain: SYS owns every base data dictionary table and should connect AS SYSDBA; SYSTEM has the DBA role granted but is a regular account, not the dictionary owner.

questions.q: Which OS group membership, by default convention, allows a local user to connect with 'sqlplus / as sysdba' without a password?
options: The dba OS group
The Administrators group on any operating system
Any group, since OS authentication ignores group membership
The oracle_users group, which is hardcoded and cannot be changed
questions.explain: Membership in the local dba OS group is what OS authentication checks for local SYSDBA connections.

questions.q: What is the real best practice for day-to-day Oracle DBA work, per this lesson?
options: Create named, individual DBA accounts with the DBA role granted, rather than doing routine work as SYS or SYSTEM
Always connect as SYS since it has every privilege and saves setup time
Share a single SYSTEM password among the whole DBA team for simplicity
Disable authentication entirely on internal networks
questions.explain: Named per-person DBA accounts keep actions attributable and avoid routine reliance on the two powerful default accounts.
